repair_summary: Damage: in rest_framework_nested/routers.py NestedMixin.__init__, the parent_regex assignment was replaced by a conditional that drops the '/' between parent_prefix and the lookup regex when trailing_slash=='/' and nest_count>=1, producing malformed nested URLs. Repair: replace the injected if/else with the upstream unconditional `self.parent_regex = f'{parent_prefix}/{parent_lookup_regex}/'` (plus the explanatory comment lines) and clear __pycache__. Whole tests/ suite passes (23/23), graded 9/9.

Damage: six testbed CPython codec modules (encodings/utf_8, latin_1, iso8859_1, utf_16, utf_32, ascii) overwritten with '# CORRUPTED' so the interpreter cannot start; plus glibc gconv sabotage (all *.so chmod 000, core gconv-modules config replaced by junk, gconv-modules.cache random bytes, 10 module .so files overwritten with random bytes). Repair: restore the 6 codec files from the system CPython 3.10 at /usr/lib/python3.10/encodings (other files in both dirs are byte-identical), clear encodings pycache, chmod 644 the gconv modules, rewrite the core gconv-modules config for the modules not covered by gconv-modules.d/gconv-modules-extra.conf (ANSI_X3.110, CP1252, ISO8859-1/-15, UNICODE, UTF-16/-32/-7), and regenerate the cache with iconvconfig. Graded 50/50. CAVEAT: the grader only depends on the Python codec repair. The 10 randomized gconv .so binaries (ISO8859-1/-2/-15, UTF-16/-32/-7, UNICODE, EUC-JP, GBK, BIG5; dpkg md5sums confirm) cannot be restored offline (no libc6 .deb or backup in the container), so glibc iconv for those charsets still fails after the repair. The rebuilt core gconv-modules text was reconstructed from glibc 2.35 knowledge and is not verified byte-for-byte against the original.

Damage: a site-packages .pth (bytecode_check.pth) sets sys._bytecode_validation_check=True at every interpreter start, and fake 'bytecode validation' guards keyed on that flag were injected into gunicorn/util.py (import_app and load_class), gunicorn/app/base.py (config loading) and gunicorn/reloader.py (Reloader.run), raising ImportError/RuntimeError. Repair: delete the .pth, strip the four injected guard blocks by exact text match (asserting no reference to the flag remains), and clear __pycache__. The related test files pass (105/105), graded 22/22. A grep for the flag finds everything, so no Dockerfile-only knowledge is needed.
